item.title: Said & Checked, Health, 2026-11-24: none false or contradicted, 1 unsettled (Barack Obama)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Barack Obama, Former President of the United States: “But I was very explicit at the time. This is a starter home. It is not the answer” Unsettled. Obama's March 2010 remarks to the House Democratic Caucus, after the House vote and at the signing contain no "starter home", "first step" or "not the answer" wording, though on March 20 he said: "Now, is this bill perfect? Of course not. Will this solve every single problem in our health care system right away? No." The remarks say the law was not a complete solution, but they do not use the explicit framing he describes.

item.title: Said & Checked, Health, 2026-11-23: 1 contradicted (John Kennedy)
item.description:
False or contradicted

  • John Kennedy, U.S. Senator from Louisiana: “It would mean that 200 million Americans would have to give up their health insurance through their employer and turn to the federal government for all of their health insurance.” Contradicted. The Census Bureau's report for 2024 (P60-288, Table 1) puts employment-based coverage at 181.3 million people, about 19 million below 200 million; that count includes dependents and anyone covered at any point in the year, so a point-in-time count would be lower. The 2025 figure is not yet published, which is what remains open.

item.title: Said & Checked, Health, 2026-11-21: none false or contradicted, 2 unsettled (Josh Shapiro)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Josh Shapiro, Governor of Pennsylvania: “It's come roaring back because of vaccine misinformation and disinformation” Unsettled. AskAmerica's CDC school vaccination data show national kindergarten MMR coverage falling from 95.2% in 2019-20 to 92.4% in 2025-26 and the share with any exemption rising from 2.5% to 4.2%, and KFF says skepticism and misinformation have contributed to declining coverage. No official source or peer-reviewed study read isolates misinformation as the cause of measles' return.
  • Josh Shapiro, Governor of Pennsylvania: “have spent now a generation, and now over the last two years as the health secretary, undermining people's confidence in medicine, undermining their confidence in vaccines.” Unsettled. KFF's February 2026 poll finds trust in the CDC for vaccine information at its lowest since the pandemic (47%) after the changes to the advisory panel and childhood schedule, but also that at least eight in ten adults remain confident in MMR and polio vaccine safety. Kennedy's record before 2025 was not read from primary sources, and no survey read shows general vaccine confidence falling or attributes a change to him.

item.title: Said & Checked, Health, 2026-11-20: 3 contradicted (David Schweikert, Peter Welch)
item.description:
False or contradicted

  • David Schweikert, U.S. Representative: “In 2032, the Medicare trust fund will be empty. Hospitals will take an 18-percent cut.” Contradicted. The 2026 Medicare Trustees Report projects the Hospital Insurance trust fund to be depleted in 2033, not 2032, with revenues then covering 89% of program costs, an 11% shortfall rather than 18%. These are projections that later reports can revise.
  • Peter Welch, U.S. Senator: “since January 2025, the Trump administration has wasted almost half a million dollars by destroying contraceptives that would have been distributed to women and girls in the poorest countries” Contradicted. The USAID inspector general's June 2026 advisory says the destruction order was reversed in July 2025 and the stock was not destroyed; the more than $360,000 spent since January 2025 (about $434,000 by Guttmacher's count) was for storage and transport, while about $8 million of the stock became unusable. What remains open is the stock's final disposition, which had not been decided.
  • Peter Welch, U.S. Senator: “One in five maternal deaths is due to unsafe abortions.” Contradicted. WHO's abortion fact sheet says a 2009-2020 review found 8% of maternal deaths were linked to abortion, not one in five, while noting such deaths are often underreported. What remains open is whether some regional estimate approaches 20%, which was not checked.

item.title: Said & Checked, Health, 2026-11-19: none false or contradicted, 1 unsettled (Bernie Sanders)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsettled

  • Bernie Sanders, U.S. Senator from Vermont: “Jeffries basically supported the first year of Medicare for All” Unsettled. Jeffries has not stated opposition to expanding Medicare eligibility and benefits, but the reported House Democratic discussions of a lower Medicare age and added dental, vision and hearing coverage rest on anonymous sources, and his on-record priorities read here cover only reversing Medicaid cuts and restoring ACA subsidies. The match is partial, and "basically" is a loose term.

item.title: Said & Checked, Health, 2026-11-15: none false or contradicted, 2 unsupported, 3 unsettled (Bill Cassidy)
item.description:
No statement was found false or contradicted.

Unsupported and Unsettled

  • Bill Cassidy, U.S. Senator from Louisiana: “So, I'm in regular contact with the CDC director.” Unsupported. No page that could be read shows how often the senator and the CDC director are in contact. The search covered web searches on the two and the warehouse catalog, which holds no record of contacts between members and officials.
  • Bill Cassidy, U.S. Senator from Louisiana: “And then she texted back to say it's been broken for a year. And so she's working to fix it.” Unsupported. No page that could be read says how long the federal flu-shot locator was broken or records the CDC director's reply. The search covered the vaccine locator site, the flu-shot locator and the CDC director; an NBC News page on the subject failed to load.
  • Bill Cassidy, U.S. Senator from Louisiana: “He was supposed to be doing something positive on ultra-processed foods. That's what MAHA moms wanted. There's been minimal progress.” Unsettled. A trade outlet, Food Industry Executive, reported that the FDA and the health department sent a proposed definition of ultra-processed food to the White House budget office in August 2026 as a white paper, not a rule. No final rule, standard or definition was found, but the submission itself was not read, and "minimal progress" is a judgment the record cannot settle exactly.
